# InfraFund dashboard (front-pro)

## Mission

Document and operationalize the InfraFund dashboard (front-pro) style foundations extracted from Figma so teams can build consistent interfaces quickly.

## Brand

- Product/brand: InfraFund dashboard (front-pro)
- Audience: Designers and engineers building this product
- Product surface: web app

## Style Foundations

- Visual style: clean, token-driven, functional
- Typography scale: Headline 1, Headline 2, Headline 3, Headline 4, Headline 5, Headline 6, Sidebar, Navbar, Navbar-selected, Subtitle, Label, Body 1, Body 2, Button
- Color palette: color/gray/50, color/gray/100, color/gray/200, color/gray/300, color/gray/400, color/gray/500, color/gray/600, color/gray/700, color/gray/800, color/gray/900, color/brand/primary, color/brand/primary-hover, color/brand/primary-pressed, color/brand/primary-disabled
- Spacing scale: Primitives/spacing/2xs, Primitives/spacing/xs, Primitives/spacing/sm, Primitives/spacing/md, Primitives/spacing/lg, Primitives/spacing/xl, Primitives/spacing/2xl, Primitives/Mode 1/spacing/2xs, Primitives/Mode 1/spacing/xs, Primitives/Mode 1/spacing/sm, Primitives/Mode 1/spacing/md, Primitives/Mode 1/spacing/lg, Primitives/Mode 1/spacing/xl, Primitives/Mode 1/spacing/2xl
- Radius/shadow/motion tokens: duration-fast 120ms, duration-base 200ms, ease-standard

## Component Families

- Frame
- Component 39
- Default marker component
- Property 1=Default
- Property 1=fill
- Property 1=Group 249
- Property 1=Group 250
- DAO

## Accessibility

- Target: WCAG 2.2 AA
- Keyboard-first interactions required
- Focus-visible rules required
- Contrast constraints required

## Writing Tone

concise, confident, implementation-focused

## Rules: Do

- Use extracted color tokens before introducing one-off values: color/gray/50
- color/gray/100
- color/gray/200
- color/gray/300
- color/gray/400
- color/gray/500.
- Use these typography styles consistently: Headline 1
- Headline 2
- Headline 3
- Headline 4
- Headline 5
- Headline 6.
- Define all interaction states for interactive components: default
- hover
- focus-visible
- active
- disabled
- and loading.

## Rules: Don't

- Do not duplicate existing style tokens with one-off naming.
- Do not remove focus-visible indicators or keyboard support.
- Do not hard-code raw values where local styles or variables already exist.

## Guideline Authoring Workflow

1. Restate design intent in one sentence.
2. Define foundations and tokens.
3. Define component anatomy
4. variants
5. and interactions.
6. Add accessibility acceptance criteria.
7. Add anti-patterns and migration notes.
8. End with QA checklist.

## Required Output Structure

- Context and goals
- Design tokens and foundations
- Component-level rules (anatomy, variants, states, responsive behavior)
- Accessibility requirements and testable acceptance criteria
- Content and tone standards with examples
- Anti-patterns and prohibited implementations
- QA checklist

## Component Rule Expectations

- Include keyboard, pointer, and touch behavior.
- Include spacing and typography token requirements.
- Include long-content, overflow, and empty-state handling.

## Quality Gates

- Every non-negotiable rule uses "must".
- Every recommendation uses "should".
- Every accessibility rule is testable in implementation.
- Prefer system consistency over local visual exceptions.

## Acceptance Checklist

- Frontmatter exists with valid `name` and `description`.
- Guidance is under 500 lines for `skill.md` when possible.
- Accessibility and interaction states are explicitly documented.
- Rules are concrete, testable, and non-ambiguous.
- Output can be reused in other repositories with only variable replacement.

## TypeUI + Agentic Integration

This `SKILL.md` is intended for `typeui.sh` CLI workflows.
It can later be integrated with agentic tools including Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and similar assistants.

## Rules: Don't

- Do not duplicate existing style tokens with one-off naming.
- Do not remove focus-visible indicators or keyboard support.
- Do not hard-code raw values where local styles or variables already exist.

1. Restate design intent in one sentence.

## Component Rule Expectations

- Include keyboard, pointer, and touch behavior.
- Include spacing and typography token requirements.
- Include long-content, overflow, and empty-state handling.

## Quality Gates

- Every non-negotiable rule uses "must".
- Every recommendation uses "should".
- Every accessibility rule is testable in implementation.
- Prefer system consistency over local visual exceptions.

- Frontmatter exists with valid `name` and `description`.

# InfraFund front-pro Design System

## Context

This file defines implementation rules for the current InfraFund web app based on the local Figma file and the existing Next.js + React + Tailwind v4 codebase.

The primary goal is consistency: new pages should feel like they belong to the same product, reuse the same primitives, and avoid one-off visual decisions.

## Source of truth

- Figma file: InfraFund-local
- Reference node: contractor dashboard (`25140:14114`)
- Existing codebase tokens: `src/app/globals.css`
- Existing reusable UI: `src/components/ui/*`, `src/components/header.tsx`, `src/components/sidebar.tsx`

## Product characteristics

- Dark, cinematic dashboard UI with neon-green brand accents.
- Card-heavy layout with soft glass overlays, subtle borders, and restrained color semantics.
- Typography splits into display/navigation text with Chakra Petch and data/detail text with IBM Plex Mono.
- Large desktop-first layouts are currently the dominant design pattern.

## Core principles

- Reuse design tokens before introducing raw hex values or bespoke spacing.
- Prefer a small number of composable primitives over large page-specific styling blocks.
- Keep interaction states explicit and consistent across all clickable surfaces.
- Use semantic accent colors sparingly; primary green is the default action color.
- Treat dashboard panels, navigation items, and stat cards as repeatable system patterns.

## Design tokens

### Colors

Use these as the canonical palette:

- Brand primary: `#24FF8E`
- Brand primary hover: `#1AD87A`
- Brand primary pressed: `#11B367`
- Brand primary disabled: `#A2F4CC`
- Gray 50: `#F5F6F8`
- Gray 100: `#EDEEF2`
- Gray 200: `#DEE0E7`
- Gray 300: `#C7CAD5`
- Gray 400: `#B3B6C6`
- Gray 500: `#9FA1B5`
- Gray 600: `#8A89A2`
- Gray 700: `#77768C`
- Gray 800: `#616172`
- Gray 900: `#51515E`
- Success: `#22C55E`
- Warning: `#FACC15`
- Error: `#EF4444`
- Info: `#3B82F6`
- Card background: `#151E2F80`
- Card border: `#FFFFFF1A`
- Selected background: `#1F2A40`

### Project token mapping

These should stay aligned with `src/app/globals.css`:

- `--color-primary`
- `--color-primary-hover`
- `--color-primary-pressed`
- `--color-primary-disabled`
- `--color-gray-50` through `--color-gray-900`
- `--color-success`
- `--color-warning`
- `--color-error`
- `--color-info`
- `--color-card-bg`
- `--color-card-bg-border`
- `--color-card-border`
- `--color-card-selected-bg`

### Typography

Use Chakra Petch for interface hierarchy and IBM Plex Mono for supporting detail.

#### Chakra Petch roles

- Headline 4: 31px, regular, tracking 0.25px
- Headline 6: 18px, medium, tracking 0.15px
- Sidebar/Nav: 16px, regular, tracking 0.15px
- Button: 14px, semibold, tracking 1.25px
- Large dashboard hero/title usage may scale to 40px bold when matching Figma page headers

#### IBM Plex Mono roles

- Body 1: 14px, regular, line-height 180%, tracking 0.5px
- Label: 16px, medium
- Body 2 / metadata: 12px, regular
- Wallet/address and supporting system text should remain monospace

### Spacing scale

Canonical spacing tokens:

- 4
- 8
- 12
- 16
- 24
- 32
- 48

Map all new spacing choices back to this scale where possible.

### Radius and effects

Current visual language inferred from Figma:

- Nav active item radius: 12px
- Standard inner card radius: 8px
- Panel/stat card radius: 20px
- Sidebar shell radius: 40px
- Avatar radius: fully rounded
- Glass surfaces should use blur and transparent dark fills instead of opaque flat fills when matching dashboard shells

## Layout system

### App shell

The main authenticated shell consists of:

- Full-screen dark background
- Two blurred background glow ellipses
- Left persistent rounded sidebar
- Top header row with page title and utility/account actions
- Main content area with generous horizontal spacing

### Content rhythm

- Page header sits above content blocks with large top spacing.
- Primary dashboard content uses horizontal card rows followed by stacked feature panels.
- Use 16px gaps inside dense groups and 24px+ gaps between major sections.
- Maintain strong alignment between content start and header title start.

## Component rules

### Sidebar

Sidebar must:

- Use Chakra Petch for nav labels.
- Present one clearly selected destination using selected background plus primary text/icon.
- Default non-active items should use gray-300/400 tones.
- Use 24px icons and 16px label text for standard navigation entries.
- Keep internal nav item padding at 16px.
- Preserve soft-glass styling on the sidebar container.

Sidebar should:

- Be driven by data structures, not repeated hardcoded JSX.
- Support role-based nav groups by configuration, not separate component forks.

### Header

Header must:

- Keep page title visually dominant.
- Place utility actions and wallet/account controls on the right.
- Use icon-only utilities before wallet/account identity.
- Keep wallet/account information compact and horizontally aligned.

Header should:

- Separate page identity from session identity.
- Allow role labels or greeting metadata under or beside the title when the page design requires it.

### Cards and panels

InfraFund uses three recurring card families:

#### 1. Stat cards

Used for top-level KPIs.

Stat cards must:

- Use glass/dark background with subtle border.
- Use 24px inner padding.
- Use Chakra Petch for label and value.
- Use semantic color only on the value or linked action when emphasis is needed.

#### 2. Content panels

Used for sections such as reports, messages, milestones, and project summary areas.

Content panels must:

- Use the same dark/glass surface family.
- Have stronger internal hierarchy than stat cards.
- Separate title, metadata, body, and CTA zones clearly.

#### 3. Nested item cards

Used for task rows and compact records inside larger panels.

Nested item cards must:

- Use a darker opaque inner fill than the parent panel.
- Keep radius smaller than parent panels.
- Reserve semantic colors for status pills, progress, and links.

### Buttons and links

Buttons must:

- Use Chakra Petch semibold 14px styling for primary action labels.
- Define default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, and loading states.
- Use primary green for default CTA emphasis.
- Keep text contrast strong when background becomes bright.

Text links inside cards should:

- Use semantic info or primary color depending on context.
- Remain visually distinct without relying only on underline.
- Preserve keyboard focus visibility.

### Status chips

Status chips are a core reusable pattern.

Status chips must:

- Be pill-shaped.
- Use tinted backgrounds plus semantic border and text color.
- Use uppercase or high-emphasis short labels consistently.
- Stay short enough to avoid collapsing layouts.

Recommended semantic mappings:

- Success/completed: green
- Warning/review needed: yellow
- Info/in progress/awaiting verification: blue
- Neutral/not started: gray
- Error/blocked: red

### Progress indicators

Progress bars must:

- Sit on dark track backgrounds.
- Use primary green as default fill unless status requires another semantic color.
- Pair the bar with nearby textual metadata such as due date or progress label.
- Avoid relying on color alone to convey state.

### Forms and inputs

Inputs must:

- Use the same dark surface family as the rest of the app.
- Have visible focus states using primary or accessible outline treatment.
- Show invalid state with clear border/message treatment.
- Use IBM Plex Mono for entered data only when the field is system/data-oriented; otherwise follow the component context.

Inputs should:

- Converge on a single shared input primitive instead of multiple ad hoc styles.
- Reuse a single dropdown/select pattern with keyboard and click-outside behavior.

### Avatars and account identity

Avatar surfaces must:

- Be circular.
- Use dark filled background distinct from surrounding shell.
- Prefer initials when no image exists.

Wallet or account labels should:

- Use IBM Plex Mono.
- Use truncation conventions consistently, e.g. `0XFF...A102`.

## Imagery

Project hero imagery in dashboard cards must:

- Be covered by a dark overlay to preserve text legibility.
- Use large headline text over the image.
- Stay decorative unless the image content is materially informative.

## Interaction behavior

All interactive components must define:

- default
- hover
- focus-visible
- active
- disabled
- loading where relevant

Keyboard rules:

- Every interactive element must be reachable by keyboard.
- Focus-visible state must be obvious on dark backgrounds.
- Menus and dropdowns must support Escape dismissal.

Pointer rules:

- Hover should increase clarity, not radically change layout.
- Cursor style should match interactivity truthfully.

## Responsive behavior

The current Figma is desktop-first, so responsive behavior must be inferred conservatively.

Until mobile designs exist:

- Preserve desktop spacing and hierarchy on large screens.
- Collapse multi-column stat rows to fewer columns on medium screens.
- Stack large split panels vertically on smaller widths.
- Avoid shrinking text below readable sizes to preserve the desktop composition.
- Sidebar behavior for smaller screens should be implemented intentionally, not as an accidental overflow result.

## Accessibility requirements

All implementations must:

- Meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast targets.
- Preserve semantic HTML for buttons, links, headings, lists, and form fields.
- Expose labels for icon-only controls.
- Avoid color-only communication for status and progress.
- Maintain visible focus indicators across all dark surfaces.
- Support keyboard dismissal for overlays, menus, and modals.

## Implementation guidance for this repo

### What to keep

- Tailwind v4 utility approach
- `globals.css` token definitions
- Existing shell structure in `main-layout.tsx`
- Reusable UI components in `src/components/ui`

### What to improve

- Replace page-specific raw colors with token-backed utilities where feasible.
- Normalize card radii and border treatments across shared primitives.
- Bring `CustomButton`, `Dropdown`, `FormInput`, and `CardView` closer to one coherent system.
- Introduce reusable dashboard primitives instead of hand-building every panel.
- Support role-specific navigation/page composition through configuration, not duplicated layouts.

### Recommended primitive set

The app should converge on reusable primitives for:

- app shell/sidebar/header
- page title block
- stat card
- glass panel
- nested row card
- status chip
- progress bar
- button
- text link / inline action
- input
- select/dropdown
- avatar/account badge

## Anti-patterns

Do not:

- Introduce new hex values when an existing token communicates the same intent.
- Mix Chakra Petch and IBM Plex Mono arbitrarily within the same UI role.
- Create role-specific pages by copying entire layouts when composition can be data-driven.
- Use inconsistent border radii for visually related components.
- Remove focus indicators to achieve a cleaner visual style.
- Treat generated Figma code as production-ready without adapting it to existing repo patterns.

## QA checklist

Before merging any UI work, verify:

- Tokens were reused instead of hardcoded one-off values.
- Typography choices match the intended role.
- Cards use the correct family and radius.
- Selected, hover, focus, disabled, and active states exist.
- Keyboard navigation works for menus, buttons, and dropdowns.
- Status colors are semantically correct and not the only cue.
- Layout remains aligned with the authenticated app shell.
- New components are reusable and not overly page-specific.

## Figma reference

- neon-green primary accents
- Chakra Petch for interface hierarchy
- IBM Plex Mono for data, metadata, and wallet/system text
- rounded panels and layered dark surfaces
- restrained semantic color usage for warning, info, success, and error states

## Non-negotiable implementation rules

- Must reuse repo tokens before introducing new raw values.
- Must adapt Figma output to the existing Next.js + React + Tailwind v4 stack.
- Must prefer reusable primitives over page-specific duplicated markup.

### Colors

- `--color-primary`
- `--color-primary-hover`
- `--color-primary-pressed`
- `--color-primary-disabled`

- `--color-success`

- `--color-card-bg-border`
- `--color-card-border`

Do not invent nearby greens, blues, or grays when these already cover the requirement.

### Typography

Use typography by role:

- Chakra Petch for page titles, section titles, nav labels, buttons, and high-emphasis interface text
- IBM Plex Mono for form data, metadata, wallet addresses, timestamps, labels, and system/supporting copy

Default expected styles:

- page title: Chakra Petch bold, around 40px when matching dashboard headers
- section/stat label: Chakra Petch medium 18px
- nav label: Chakra Petch 16px
- button label: Chakra Petch semibold 14px with tracked lettering
- supporting body/meta: IBM Plex Mono 12px to 14px

### Spacing and radius

Prefer the spacing scale 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48.

Prefer these radius tiers:

- 8px for nested items
- 12px for selected nav or compact highlighted surfaces
- 20px for major cards
- 40px for large shell containers like the sidebar

## Core component families

When writing guidance, organize components into these families:

1. App shell
2. Sidebar navigation
3. Header / account area
4. Stat cards
5. Glass panels
6. Nested item cards
7. Status chips
8. Progress indicators
9. Buttons and text actions
10. Inputs and selects
11. Avatars / wallet identity

For each family, define:

- anatomy
- typography
- spacing
- color usage
- interactive states
- accessibility expectations
- responsive behavior

## Interaction and accessibility rules

Every interactive component must define:

- default
- hover
- focus-visible
- active
- disabled
- loading when relevant

Every design rule set must include testable accessibility requirements:

- WCAG 2.2 AA contrast expectations
- keyboard reachability
- visible focus treatment
- icon-only labeling requirements
- non-color cues for status and progress
- Escape dismissal for overlays or menus where relevant

## Repo-specific guidance expectations

When giving implementation advice, explicitly align with the current repo by checking:

- whether a shared primitive already exists
- whether a token already exists in `globals.css`
- whether the shell layout already solves part of the page
- whether a component is currently inconsistent and should be normalized instead of copied

Favor convergence of existing components such as:

- `CustomButton`
- `Dropdown`
- `FormInput`
- `CardView`

## Output structure

When asked to generate guidance, use this structure:

1. Context and goal
2. Relevant existing repo patterns
3. Relevant Figma observations
4. Design tokens to use
5. Component-level rules
6. Interaction and accessibility requirements
7. Responsive behavior
8. Anti-patterns to avoid
9. Implementation notes for this repo
10. QA checklist

## Writing style

Write in a concise, confident, implementation-focused tone.

Use:

- "must" for non-negotiable rules
- "should" for recommendations
- direct references to file paths or component names when relevant

Avoid vague advice like "make it look modern" or "keep it clean" unless followed by a concrete, testable rule.

## Anti-patterns

Do not:

- output only token dumps without component guidance
- recommend raw Tailwind classes without tying them back to tokens/system intent
- ignore existing repo patterns and shared components
- propose inaccessible icon-only controls
- duplicate full page layouts when variation can be driven by data/configuration

## Success criteria

A good result:

- is reusable across multiple pages, not only one screen
- helps engineers decide what to build and how to structure it
- reflects both Figma and the real codebase
- gives explicit component/state/accessibility rules
- reduces ad hoc styling decisions in future work

# InfraFund design skill

## Mission

Create implementation-ready design guidance for InfraFund UI work so engineers can build new pages and components that stay aligned with the local Figma system and this repository's established front-end patterns.

## Sources of truth

Always reconcile guidance against all of the following:

- `DESIGN.md`
- `src/app/globals.css`
- shared UI in `src/components/ui/*`
- shell components such as `src/components/header.tsx`, `src/components/sidebar.tsx`, and `src/components/main-layout.tsx`
- the active Figma file and requested node

Primary Figma reference for current dashboard system:
- contractor dashboard node `25140:14114`
- file: `InfraFund-local`

## Product style summary

InfraFund is a dark, glassy, dashboard-oriented web application with:

- neon-green primary accents
- Chakra Petch for interface hierarchy
- IBM Plex Mono for data, metadata, and wallet/system text
- rounded panels and layered dark surfaces
- restrained semantic color usage for warning, info, success, and error states

## Non-negotiable implementation rules

- Must reuse repo tokens before introducing new raw values.
- Must adapt Figma output to the existing Next.js + React + Tailwind v4 stack.
- Must prefer reusable primitives over page-specific duplicated markup.
- Must preserve keyboard accessibility and visible focus states.
- Must keep role-specific variations configuration-driven when possible.
- Must treat generated Figma code as reference, not final production code.

## Token rules

### Colors

Prefer the tokens already declared in `src/app/globals.css`, especially:

- `--color-primary`
- `--color-primary-hover`
- `--color-primary-pressed`
- `--color-primary-disabled`
- `--color-gray-50` through `--color-gray-900`
- `--color-success`
- `--color-warning`
- `--color-error`
- `--color-info`
- `--color-card-bg`
- `--color-card-bg-border`
- `--color-card-border`
- `--color-card-selected-bg`

Do not invent nearby greens, blues, or grays when these already cover the requirement.

### Typography

Use typography by role:

- Chakra Petch for page titles, section titles, nav labels, buttons, and high-emphasis interface text
- IBM Plex Mono for form data, metadata, wallet addresses, timestamps, labels, and system/supporting copy

Default expected styles:

- page title: Chakra Petch bold, around 40px when matching dashboard headers
- section/stat label: Chakra Petch medium 18px
- nav label: Chakra Petch 16px
- button label: Chakra Petch semibold 14px with tracked lettering
- supporting body/meta: IBM Plex Mono 12px to 14px

### Spacing and radius

Prefer the spacing scale 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48.

Prefer these radius tiers:

- 8px for nested items
- 12px for selected nav or compact highlighted surfaces
- 20px for major cards
- 40px for large shell containers like the sidebar

## Core component families

When writing guidance, organize components into these families:

1. App shell
2. Sidebar navigation
3. Header / account area
4. Stat cards
5. Glass panels
6. Nested item cards
7. Status chips
8. Progress indicators
9. Buttons and text actions
10. Inputs and selects
11. Avatars / wallet identity

For each family, define:

- anatomy
- typography
- spacing
- color usage
- interactive states
- accessibility expectations
- responsive behavior

## Interaction and accessibility rules

Every interactive component must define:

- default
- hover
- focus-visible
- active
- disabled
- loading when relevant

Every design rule set must include testable accessibility requirements:

- WCAG 2.2 AA contrast expectations
- keyboard reachability
- visible focus treatment
- icon-only labeling requirements
- non-color cues for status and progress
- Escape dismissal for overlays or menus where relevant

## Repo-specific guidance expectations

When giving implementation advice, explicitly align with the current repo by checking:

- whether a shared primitive already exists
- whether a token already exists in `globals.css`
- whether the shell layout already solves part of the page
- whether a component is currently inconsistent and should be normalized instead of copied

Favor convergence of existing components such as:

- `CustomButton`
- `Dropdown`
- `FormInput`
- `CardView`

## Output structure

When asked to generate guidance, use this structure:

1. Context and goal
2. Relevant existing repo patterns
3. Relevant Figma observations
4. Design tokens to use
5. Component-level rules
6. Interaction and accessibility requirements
7. Responsive behavior
8. Anti-patterns to avoid
9. Implementation notes for this repo
10. QA checklist

## Writing style

Write in a concise, confident, implementation-focused tone.

Use:

- "must" for non-negotiable rules
- "should" for recommendations
- direct references to file paths or component names when relevant

Avoid vague advice like "make it look modern" or "keep it clean" unless followed by a concrete, testable rule.

## Anti-patterns

Do not:

- output only token dumps without component guidance
- recommend raw Tailwind classes without tying them back to tokens/system intent
- ignore existing repo patterns and shared components
- propose inaccessible icon-only controls
- duplicate full page layouts when variation can be driven by data/configuration

## Success criteria

A good result:

- is reusable across multiple pages, not only one screen
- helps engineers decide what to build and how to structure it
- reflects both Figma and the real codebase
- gives explicit component/state/accessibility rules
- reduces ad hoc styling decisions in future work

# InfraFund front-pro Design System

## Context

This file defines implementation rules for the current InfraFund web app based on the local Figma file and the existing Next.js + React + Tailwind v4 codebase.

The primary goal is consistency: new pages should feel like they belong to the same product, reuse the same primitives, and avoid one-off visual decisions.

## Source of truth

- Figma file: InfraFund-local
- Reference node: contractor dashboard (`25140:14114`)
- Existing codebase tokens: `src/app/globals.css`
- Existing reusable UI: `src/components/ui/*`, `src/components/header.tsx`, `src/components/sidebar.tsx`

## Product characteristics

- Dark, cinematic dashboard UI with neon-green brand accents.
- Card-heavy layout with soft glass overlays, subtle borders, and restrained color semantics.
- Typography splits into display/navigation text with Chakra Petch and data/detail text with IBM Plex Mono.
- Large desktop-first layouts are currently the dominant design pattern.

## Core principles

- Reuse design tokens before introducing raw hex values or bespoke spacing.
- Prefer a small number of composable primitives over large page-specific styling blocks.
- Keep interaction states explicit and consistent across all clickable surfaces.
- Use semantic accent colors sparingly; primary green is the default action color.
- Treat dashboard panels, navigation items, and stat cards as repeatable system patterns.

## Design tokens

### Colors

- Brand primary: `#24FF8E`
- Brand primary hover: `#1AD87A`
- Brand primary pressed: `#11B367`
- Brand primary disabled: `#A2F4CC`
- Gray 50: `#F5F6F8`
- Gray 100: `#EDEEF2`
- Gray 200: `#DEE0E7`
- Gray 300: `#C7CAD5`
- Gray 400: `#B3B6C6`
- Gray 500: `#9FA1B5`
- Gray 600: `#8A89A2`
- Gray 700: `#77768C`

- Gray 900: `#51515E`
- Success: `#22C55E`
- Warning: `#FACC15`
- Error: `#EF4444`
- Info: `#3B82F6`
- Card background: `#151E2F80`
- Card border: `#FFFFFF1A`
- Selected background: `#1F2A40`

### Project token mapping

- `--color-success`

- `--color-error`
- `--color-info`
- `--color-card-bg`
- `--color-card-bg-border`
- `--color-card-border`
- `--color-card-selected-bg`

### Typography

Use Chakra Petch for interface hierarchy and IBM Plex Mono for supporting detail.

#### Chakra Petch roles

- Headline 4: 31px, regular, tracking 0.25px
- Headline 6: 18px, medium, tracking 0.15px
- Sidebar/Nav: 16px, regular, tracking 0.15px
- Button: 14px, semibold, tracking 1.25px
- Large dashboard hero/title usage may scale to 40px bold when matching Figma page headers

#### IBM Plex Mono roles

- Body 1: 14px, regular, line-height 180%, tracking 0.5px
- Label: 16px, medium
- Body 2 / metadata: 12px, regular
- Wallet/address and supporting system text should remain monospace

### Spacing scale

Canonical spacing tokens:

- 4
- 8
- 12
- 16
- 24
- 32
- 48

Map all new spacing choices back to this scale where possible.

### Radius and effects

Current visual language inferred from Figma:

- Nav active item radius: 12px
- Standard inner card radius: 8px
- Panel/stat card radius: 20px
- Sidebar shell radius: 40px
- Avatar radius: fully rounded
- Glass surfaces should use blur and transparent dark fills instead of opaque flat fills when matching dashboard shells

## Layout system

### App shell

The main authenticated shell consists of:

- Full-screen dark background
- Two blurred background glow ellipses
- Left persistent rounded sidebar
- Top header row with page title and utility/account actions
- Main content area with generous horizontal spacing

### Content rhythm

- Page header sits above content blocks with large top spacing.
- Primary dashboard content uses horizontal card rows followed by stacked feature panels.
- Use 16px gaps inside dense groups and 24px+ gaps between major sections.
- Maintain strong alignment between content start and header title start.

## Component rules

### Sidebar

Sidebar must:

- Use Chakra Petch for nav labels.
- Present one clearly selected destination using selected background plus primary text/icon.
- Default non-active items should use gray-300/400 tones.
- Use 24px icons and 16px label text for standard navigation entries.
- Keep internal nav item padding at 16px.
- Preserve soft-glass styling on the sidebar container.

Sidebar should:

- Be driven by data structures, not repeated hardcoded JSX.
- Support role-based nav groups by configuration, not separate component forks.

### Header

Header must:

- Keep page title visually dominant.
- Place utility actions and wallet/account controls on the right.
- Use icon-only utilities before wallet/account identity.
- Keep wallet/account information compact and horizontally aligned.

Header should:

- Separate page identity from session identity.
- Allow role labels or greeting metadata under or beside the title when the page design requires it.

### Cards and panels

InfraFund uses three recurring card families:

#### 1. Stat cards

Used for top-level KPIs.

Stat cards must:

- Use glass/dark background with subtle border.
- Use 24px inner padding.
- Use Chakra Petch for label and value.
- Use semantic color only on the value or linked action when emphasis is needed.

#### 2. Content panels

Used for sections such as reports, messages, milestones, and project summary areas.

Content panels must:

- Use the same dark/glass surface family.
- Have stronger internal hierarchy than stat cards.
- Separate title, metadata, body, and CTA zones clearly.

#### 3. Nested item cards

Used for task rows and compact records inside larger panels.

Nested item cards must:

- Use a darker opaque inner fill than the parent panel.
- Keep radius smaller than parent panels.
- Reserve semantic colors for status pills, progress, and links.

### Buttons and links

Buttons must:

- Use Chakra Petch semibold 14px styling for primary action labels.
- Define default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, and loading states.
- Use primary green for default CTA emphasis.
- Keep text contrast strong when background becomes bright.

Text links inside cards should:

- Use semantic info or primary color depending on context.
- Remain visually distinct without relying only on underline.
- Preserve keyboard focus visibility.

### Status chips

Status chips are a core reusable pattern.

Status chips must:

- Be pill-shaped.
- Use tinted backgrounds plus semantic border and text color.
- Use uppercase or high-emphasis short labels consistently.
- Stay short enough to avoid collapsing layouts.

Recommended semantic mappings:

- Success/completed: green
- Warning/review needed: yellow
- Info/in progress/awaiting verification: blue
- Neutral/not started: gray
- Error/blocked: red

### Progress indicators

Progress bars must:

- Sit on dark track backgrounds.
- Use primary green as default fill unless status requires another semantic color.
- Pair the bar with nearby textual metadata such as due date or progress label.
- Avoid relying on color alone to convey state.

# InfraFund design skill

## Mission

Create implementation-ready design guidance for InfraFund UI work so
engineers can build new pages and components that stay aligned with the
local Figma system and this repository's established front-end patterns.

## Sources of truth

Always reconcile guidance against all of the following:

- `DESIGN.md`
- `src/app/globals.css`
- shared UI in `src/components/ui/*`
- shell components such as `src/components/header.tsx`, `src/components/sidebar.tsx`, and `src/components/main-layout.tsx`
- the active Figma file and requested node

Primary Figma reference for current dashboard system:

- contractor dashboard node `25140:14114`
- file: `InfraFund-local`

## Product style summary

InfraFund is a dark, glassy, dashboard-oriented web application with:

- neon-green primary accents
- Chakra Petch for interface hierarchy
- IBM Plex Mono for data, metadata, and wallet/system text
- rounded panels and layered dark surfaces
- restrained semantic color usage for warning, info, success, and error states

## Non-negotiable implementation rules

- Must reuse repo tokens before introducing new raw values.
- Must adapt Figma output to the existing Next.js + React + Tailwind v4 stack.
- Must prefer reusable primitives over page-specific duplicated markup.
- Must preserve keyboard accessibility and visible focus states.
- Must keep role-specific variations configuration-driven when possible.
- Must treat generated Figma code as reference, not final production code.

## Token rules

### Colors

Prefer the tokens already declared in `src/app/globals.css`, especially:

- `--color-primary`
- `--color-primary-hover`
- `--color-primary-pressed`
- `--color-primary-disabled`
- `--color-gray-50` through `--color-gray-900`
- `--color-success`
- `--color-warning`
- `--color-error`
- `--color-info`
- `--color-card-bg`
- `--color-card-bg-border`
- `--color-card-border`
- `--color-card-selected-bg`

Do not invent nearby greens, blues, or grays when these already cover the requirement.

### Typography

Use typography by role:

- Chakra Petch for page titles, section titles, nav labels, buttons, and high-emphasis interface text
- IBM Plex Mono for form data, metadata, wallet addresses, timestamps, labels, and system/supporting copy

Default expected styles:

- page title: Chakra Petch bold, around 40px when matching dashboard headers
- section/stat label: Chakra Petch medium 18px
- nav label: Chakra Petch 16px
- button label: Chakra Petch semibold 14px with tracked lettering
- supporting body/meta: IBM Plex Mono 12px to 14px

### Spacing and radius

Prefer the spacing scale 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48.

Prefer these radius tiers:

- 8px for nested items
- 12px for selected nav or compact highlighted surfaces
- 20px for major cards
- 40px for large shell containers like the sidebar

## Core component families

When writing guidance, organize components into these families:

1. App shell
2. Sidebar navigation
3. Header / account area
4. Stat cards
5. Glass panels
6. Nested item cards
7. Status chips
8. Progress indicators
9. Buttons and text actions
10. Inputs and selects
11. Avatars / wallet identity

For each family, define:

- anatomy
- typography
- spacing
- color usage
- interactive states
- accessibility expectations
- responsive behavior

## Interaction and accessibility rules

Every interactive component must define:

- default
- hover
- focus-visible
- active
- disabled
- loading when relevant

Every design rule set must include testable accessibility requirements:

- WCAG 2.2 AA contrast expectations
- keyboard reachability
- visible focus treatment
- icon-only labeling requirements
- non-color cues for status and progress
- Escape dismissal for overlays or menus where relevant

## Repo-specific guidance expectations

When giving implementation advice, explicitly align with the current repo by checking:

- whether a shared primitive already exists
- whether a token already exists in `globals.css`
- whether the shell layout already solves part of the page
- whether a component is currently inconsistent and should be normalized instead of copied

Favor convergence of existing components such as:

- `CustomButton`
- `Dropdown`
- `FormInput`
- `CardView`

## Output structure

When asked to generate guidance, use this structure:

1. Context and goal
2. Relevant existing repo patterns
3. Relevant Figma observations
4. Design tokens to use
5. Component-level rules
6. Interaction and accessibility requirements
7. Responsive behavior
8. Anti-patterns to avoid
9. Implementation notes for this repo
10. QA checklist

## Writing style

Write in a concise, confident, implementation-focused tone.

Use:

- "must" for non-negotiable rules
- "should" for recommendations
- direct references to file paths or component names when relevant

Avoid vague advice like "make it look modern" or "keep it clean" unless followed by a concrete, testable rule.

## Anti-patterns

Do not:

- output only token dumps without component guidance
- recommend raw Tailwind classes without tying them back to tokens/system intent
- ignore existing repo patterns and shared components
- propose inaccessible icon-only controls
- duplicate full page layouts when variation can be driven by data/configuration

## Success criteria

A good result:

- is reusable across multiple pages, not only one screen
- helps engineers decide what to build and how to structure it
- reflects both Figma and the real codebase
- gives explicit component/state/accessibility rules
- reduces ad hoc styling decisions in future work

- Headline 4: 31px, regular, tracking 0.25px
- Headline 6: 18px, medium, tracking 0.15px
- Sidebar/Nav: 16px, regular, tracking 0.15px

#### IBM Plex Mono roles

- Body 1: 14px, regular, line-height 180%, tracking 0.5px
- Label: 16px, medium
- Body 2 / metadata: 12px, regular
- Wallet/address and supporting system text should remain monospace

### Spacing scale

Canonical spacing tokens:

- 4
- 8
- 12
- 16
- 24
- 32
- 48

Map all new spacing choices back to this scale where possible.

### Radius and effects

Current visual language inferred from Figma:

- Nav active item radius: 12px
- Standard inner card radius: 8px
- Panel/stat card radius: 20px
- Sidebar shell radius: 40px
- Avatar radius: fully rounded
- Glass surfaces should use blur and transparent dark fills instead of opaque flat fills when matching dashboard shells

## Layout system

### App shell

The main authenticated shell consists of:

- Full-screen dark background
- Two blurred background glow ellipses
- Left persistent rounded sidebar
- Top header row with page title and utility/account actions
- Main content area with generous horizontal spacing

### Content rhythm

- Page header sits above content blocks with large top spacing.
- Primary dashboard content uses horizontal card rows followed by stacked feature panels.
- Use 16px gaps inside dense groups and 24px+ gaps between major sections.
- Maintain strong alignment between content start and header title start.

## Component rules

### Sidebar

Sidebar must:

- Use Chakra Petch for nav labels.
- Present one clearly selected destination using selected background plus primary text/icon.
- Default non-active items should use gray-300/400 tones.
- Use 24px icons and 16px label text for standard navigation entries.
- Keep internal nav item padding at 16px.
- Preserve soft-glass styling on the sidebar container.

Sidebar should:

- Be driven by data structures, not repeated hardcoded JSX.
- Support role-based nav groups by configuration, not separate component forks.

### Header

Header must:

- Keep page title visually dominant.
- Place utility actions and wallet/account controls on the right.
- Use icon-only utilities before wallet/account identity.
- Keep wallet/account information compact and horizontally aligned.

Header should:

- Separate page identity from session identity.
- Allow role labels or greeting metadata under or beside the title when the page design requires it.

### Cards and panels

InfraFund uses three recurring card families:

#### 1. Stat cards

Used for top-level KPIs.

Stat cards must:

- Use glass/dark background with subtle border.
- Use 24px inner padding.
- Use Chakra Petch for label and value.
- Use semantic color only on the value or linked action when emphasis is needed.

#### 2. Content panels

Used for sections such as reports, messages, milestones, and project summary areas.

Content panels must:

- Use the same dark/glass surface family.
- Have stronger internal hierarchy than stat cards.
- Separate title, metadata, body, and CTA zones clearly.

#### 3. Nested item cards

Used for task rows and compact records inside larger panels.


<system-reminder>[Showing lines 101-220 of 411 total lines]</system-reminder>

Nested item cards must:

- Use a darker opaque inner fill than the parent panel.
- Keep radius smaller than parent panels.
- Reserve semantic colors for status pills, progress, and links.

### Buttons and links

Buttons must:

- Use Chakra Petch semibold 14px styling for primary action labels.
- Define default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, and loading states.
- Use primary green for default CTA emphasis.
- Keep text contrast strong when background becomes bright.

Text links inside cards should:

- Use semantic info or primary color depending on context.
- Remain visually distinct without relying only on underline.
- Preserve keyboard focus visibility.

### Status chips

Status chips are a core reusable pattern.

Status chips must:

- Be pill-shaped.
- Use tinted backgrounds plus semantic border and text color.
- Use uppercase or high-emphasis short labels consistently.
- Stay short enough to avoid collapsing layouts.

Recommended semantic mappings:

- Success/completed: green
- Warning/review needed: yellow
- Info/in progress/awaiting verification: blue
- Neutral/not started: gray
- Error/blocked: red

### Progress indicators

Progress bars must:

- Sit on dark track backgrounds.
- Use primary green as default fill unless status requires another semantic color.
- Pair the bar with nearby textual metadata such as due date or progress label.
- Avoid relying on color alone to convey state.

### Forms and inputs

Inputs must:

- Use the same dark surface family as the rest of the app.
- Have visible focus states using primary or accessible outline treatment.
- Show invalid state with clear border/message treatment.
- Use IBM Plex Mono for entered data only when the field is system/data-oriented; otherwise follow the component context.

Inputs should:

- Converge on a single shared input primitive instead of multiple ad hoc styles.
- Reuse a single dropdown/select pattern with keyboard and click-outside behavior.

### Avatars and account identity

Avatar surfaces must:

- Be circular.
- Use dark filled background distinct from surrounding shell.
- Prefer initials when no image exists.

Wallet or account labels should:

- Use IBM Plex Mono.
- Use truncation conventions consistently, e.g. `0XFF...A102`.

## Imagery

Project hero imagery in dashboard cards must:

- Be covered by a dark overlay to preserve text legibility.
- Use large headline text over the image.
- Stay decorative unless the image content is materially informative.

## Interaction behavior

All interactive components must define:

- default
- hover
- focus-visible
- active
- disabled
- loading where relevant

Keyboard rules:

- Every interactive element must be reachable by keyboard.
- Focus-visible state must be obvious on dark backgrounds.
- Menus and dropdowns must support Escape dismissal.

Pointer rules:

- Hover should increase clarity, not radically change layout.
- Cursor style should match interactivity truthfully.

## Responsive behavior

The current Figma is desktop-first, so responsive behavior must be inferred conservatively.

Until mobile designs exist:

- Preserve desktop spacing and hierarchy on large screens.
- Collapse multi-column stat rows to fewer columns on medium screens.
- Stack large split panels vertically on smaller widths.
- Avoid shrinking text below readable sizes to preserve the desktop composition.
- Sidebar behavior for smaller screens should be implemented intentionally, not as an accidental overflow result.

## Accessibility requirements

All implementations must:

- Meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast targets.
- Preserve semantic HTML for buttons, links, headings, lists, and form fields.
- Expose labels for icon-only controls.
- Avoid color-only communication for status and progress.
- Maintain visible focus indicators across all dark surfaces.
- Support keyboard dismissal for overlays, menus, and modals.

## Implementation guidance for this repo

### What to keep

- Tailwind v4 utility approach
- `globals.css` token definitions
- Existing shell structure in `main-layout.tsx`
- Reusable UI components in `src/components/ui`

### What to improve

- Replace page-specific raw colors with token-backed utilities where feasible.
- Normalize card radii and border treatments across shared primitives.
- Bring `CustomButton`, `Dropdown`, `FormInput`, and `CardView` closer to one coherent system.
- Introduce reusable dashboard primitives instead of hand-building every panel.
- Support role-specific navigation/page composition through configuration, not duplicated layouts.

### Recommended primitive set

The app should converge on reusable primitives for:

- app shell/sidebar/header
- page title block
- stat card
- glass panel
- nested row card
- status chip
- progress bar
- button
- text link / inline action
- input
- select/dropdown
- avatar/account badge

## Anti-patterns

Do not:

- Introduce new hex values when an existing token communicates the same intent.
- Mix Chakra Petch and IBM Plex Mono arbitrarily within the same UI role.
- Create role-specific pages by copying entire layouts when composition can be data-driven.
- Use inconsistent border radii for visually related components.
- Remove focus indicators to achieve a cleaner visual style.
- Treat generated Figma code as production-ready without adapting it to existing repo patterns.

## QA checklist

Before merging any UI work, verify:

- Tokens were reused instead of hardcoded one-off values.
- Typography choices match the intended role.
- Cards use the correct family and radius.
- Selected, hover, focus, disabled, and active states exist.
- Keyboard navigation works for menus, buttons, and dropdowns.
- Status colors are semantically correct and not the only cue.
- Layout remains aligned with the authenticated app shell.
- New components are reusable and not overly page-specific.

# InfraFund design skill

Create implementation-ready design guidance for InfraFund UI work so

## Sources of truth

Always reconcile guidance against all of the following:

- `DESIGN.md`
- `src/app/globals.css`
- shared UI in `src/components/ui/*`
- shell components such as `src/components/header.tsx`,
  `src/components/sidebar.tsx`, and
  `src/components/main-layout.tsx`
- the active Figma file and requested node

Primary Figma reference for current dashboard system:

- contractor dashboard node `25140:14114`
- file: `InfraFund-local`

## Product style summary

InfraFund is a dark, glassy, dashboard-oriented web application with:

- neon-green primary accents
- Chakra Petch for interface hierarchy
- IBM Plex Mono for data, metadata, and wallet/system text
- rounded panels and layered dark surfaces
- restrained semantic color usage for warning, info, success, and error states

## Non-negotiable implementation rules

- Must reuse repo tokens before introducing new raw values.
- Must adapt Figma output to the existing Next.js + React + Tailwind v4 stack.
- Must prefer reusable primitives over page-specific duplicated markup.
- Must preserve keyboard accessibility and visible focus states.
- Must keep role-specific variations configuration-driven when possible.
- Must treat generated Figma code as reference, not final production code.

## Token rules

### Colors

Prefer the tokens already declared in `src/app/globals.css`, especially:

- `--color-primary`
- `--color-primary-hover`
- `--color-primary-pressed`
- `--color-primary-disabled`
- `--color-gray-50` through `--color-gray-900`
- `--color-success`
- `--color-warning`
- `--color-error`
- `--color-info`
- `--color-card-bg`
- `--color-card-bg-border`
- `--color-card-border`
- `--color-card-selected-bg`

Do not invent nearby greens, blues, or grays when these already cover
the requirement.

### Typography

Use typography by role:

# InfraFund front-pro Design System

## Context

This file defines implementation rules for the current InfraFund web app based on the local Figma file and the existing Next.js + React + Tailwind v4 codebase.

The primary goal is consistency: new pages should feel like they belong to the same product, reuse the same primitives, and avoid one-off visual decisions.

## Source of truth

- Figma file: InfraFund-local
- Reference node: contractor dashboard (`25140:14114`)
- Existing codebase tokens: `src/app/globals.css`
- Existing reusable UI: `src/components/ui/*`, `src/components/header.tsx`, `src/components/sidebar.tsx`

## Product characteristics

- Dark, cinematic dashboard UI with neon-green brand accents.
- Card-heavy layout with soft glass overlays, subtle borders, and restrained color semantics.
- Typography splits into display/navigation text with Chakra Petch and data/detail text with IBM Plex Mono.
- Large desktop-first layouts are currently the dominant design pattern.

## Core principles

- Reuse design tokens before introducing raw hex values or bespoke spacing.
- Prefer a small number of composable primitives over large page-specific styling blocks.
- Keep interaction states explicit and consistent across all clickable surfaces.
- Use semantic accent colors sparingly; primary green is the default action color.
- Treat dashboard panels, navigation items, and stat cards as repeatable system patterns.

## Design tokens

### Colors

Use these as the canonical palette:

- Brand primary: `#24FF8E`
- Brand primary hover: `#1AD87A`
- Brand primary pressed: `#11B367`
- Brand primary disabled: `#A2F4CC`
- Gray 50: `#F5F6F8`
- Gray 100: `#EDEEF2`
- Gray 200: `#DEE0E7`
- Gray 300: `#C7CAD5`
- Gray 400: `#B3B6C6`
- Gray 500: `#9FA1B5`
- Gray 600: `#8A89A2`
- Gray 700: `#77768C`
- Gray 800: `#616172`
- Gray 900: `#51515E`
- Success: `#22C55E`
- Warning: `#FACC15`
- Error: `#EF4444`
- Info: `#3B82F6`
- Card background: `#151E2F80`
- Card border: `#FFFFFF1A`
- Selected background: `#1F2A40`

### Project token mapping

These should stay aligned with `src/app/globals.css`:

- `--color-primary`
- `--color-primary-hover`
- `--color-primary-pressed`
- `--color-primary-disabled`
- `--color-gray-50` through `--color-gray-900`
- `--color-success`
- `--color-warning`
- `--color-error`
- `--color-info`
- `--color-card-bg`
- `--color-card-bg-border`
- `--color-card-border`
- `--color-card-selected-bg`

### Typography

Use Chakra Petch for interface hierarchy and IBM Plex Mono for supporting detail.

#### Chakra Petch roles

- Headline 4: 31px, regular, tracking 0.25px
- Headline 6: 18px, medium, tracking 0.15px
- Sidebar/Nav: 16px, regular, tracking 0.15px
- Button: 14px, semibold, tracking 1.25px
- Large dashboard hero/title usage may scale to 40px bold when matching Figma page headers

#### IBM Plex Mono roles

- Body 1: 14px, regular, line-height 180%, tracking 0.5px
- Label: 16px, medium
- Body 2 / metadata: 12px, regular
- Wallet/address and supporting system text should remain monospace

### Spacing scale

Canonical spacing tokens:

- 4
- 8
- 12
- 16
- 24
- 32
- 48

Map all new spacing choices back to this scale where possible.

### Radius and effects

Current visual language inferred from Figma:

- Nav active item radius: 12px
- Standard inner card radius: 8px
- Panel/stat card radius: 20px
- Sidebar shell radius: 40px
- Avatar radius: fully rounded
- Glass surfaces should use blur and transparent dark fills instead of opaque flat fills when matching dashboard shells

## Layout system

### App shell

The main authenticated shell consists of:

- Full-screen dark background
- Two blurred background glow ellipses
- Left persistent rounded sidebar
- Top header row with page title and utility/account actions
- Main content area with generous horizontal spacing

### Content rhythm

- Page header sits above content blocks with large top spacing.
- Primary dashboard content uses horizontal card rows followed by stacked feature panels.
- Use 16px gaps inside dense groups and 24px+ gaps between major sections.
- Maintain strong alignment between content start and header title start.

## Component rules

### Sidebar

Sidebar must:

- Use Chakra Petch for nav labels.
- Present one clearly selected destination using selected background plus primary text/icon.
- Default non-active items should use gray-300/400 tones.
- Use 24px icons and 16px label text for standard navigation entries.
- Keep internal nav item padding at 16px.
- Preserve soft-glass styling on the sidebar container.

Sidebar should:

- Be driven by data structures, not repeated hardcoded JSX.
- Support role-based nav groups by configuration, not separate component forks.

### Header

Header must:

- Keep page title visually dominant.
- Place utility actions and wallet/account controls on the right.
- Use icon-only utilities before wallet/account identity.
- Keep wallet/account information compact and horizontally aligned.

Header should:

- Separate page identity from session identity.
- Allow role labels or greeting metadata under or beside the title when the page design requires it.

### Cards and panels

InfraFund uses three recurring card families:

#### 1. Stat cards

Used for top-level KPIs.

Stat cards must:

- Use glass/dark background with subtle border.
- Use 24px inner padding.
- Use Chakra Petch for label and value.
- Use semantic color only on the value or linked action when emphasis is needed.

#### 2. Content panels

Used for sections such as reports, messages, milestones, and project summary areas.

Content panels must:

- Use the same dark/glass surface family.
- Have stronger internal hierarchy than stat cards.
- Separate title, metadata, body, and CTA zones clearly.

#### 3. Nested item cards

Used for task rows and compact records inside larger panels.

Nested item cards must:

- Use a darker opaque inner fill than the parent panel.
- Keep radius smaller than parent panels.
- Reserve semantic colors for status pills, progress, and links.

### Buttons and links

Buttons must:

- Use Chakra Petch semibold 14px styling for primary action labels.
- Define default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, and loading states.
- Use primary green for default CTA emphasis.
- Keep text contrast strong when background becomes bright.

Text links inside cards should:

- Use semantic info or primary color depending on context.
- Remain visually distinct without relying only on underline.
- Preserve keyboard focus visibility.

### Status chips

Status chips are a core reusable pattern.

Status chips must:

- Be pill-shaped.
- Use tinted backgrounds plus semantic border and text color.
- Use uppercase or high-emphasis short labels consistently.
- Stay short enough to avoid collapsing layouts.

Recommended semantic mappings:

- Success/completed: green
- Warning/review needed: yellow
- Info/in progress/awaiting verification: blue
- Neutral/not started: gray
- Error/blocked: red

### Progress indicators

Progress bars must:

- Sit on dark track backgrounds.
- Use primary green as default fill unless status requires another semantic color.
- Pair the bar with nearby textual metadata such as due date or progress label.
- Avoid relying on color alone to convey state.

### Forms and inputs

Inputs must:

- Use the same dark surface family as the rest of the app.
- Have visible focus states using primary or accessible outline treatment.
- Show invalid state with clear border/message treatment.
- Use IBM Plex Mono for entered data only when the field is system/data-oriented; otherwise follow the component context.

Inputs should:

- Converge on a single shared input primitive instead of multiple ad hoc styles.
- Reuse a single dropdown/select pattern with keyboard and click-outside behavior.

### Avatars and account identity

Avatar surfaces must:

- Be circular.
- Use dark filled background distinct from surrounding shell.
- Prefer initials when no image exists.

Wallet or account labels should:

- Use IBM Plex Mono.
- Use truncation conventions consistently, e.g. `0XFF...A102`.

## Imagery

Project hero imagery in dashboard cards must:

- Be covered by a dark overlay to preserve text legibility.
- Use large headline text over the image.
- Stay decorative unless the image content is materially informative.

## Interaction behavior

All interactive components must define:

- default
- hover
- focus-visible
- active
- disabled
- loading where relevant

Keyboard rules:

- Every interactive element must be reachable by keyboard.
- Focus-visible state must be obvious on dark backgrounds.
- Menus and dropdowns must support Escape dismissal.

Pointer rules:

- Hover should increase clarity, not radically change layout.
- Cursor style should match interactivity truthfully.

## Responsive behavior

The current Figma is desktop-first, so responsive behavior must be inferred conservatively.

Until mobile designs exist:

- Preserve desktop spacing and hierarchy on large screens.
- Collapse multi-column stat rows to fewer columns on medium screens.
- Stack large split panels vertically on smaller widths.
- Avoid shrinking text below readable sizes to preserve the desktop composition.
- Sidebar behavior for smaller screens should be implemented intentionally, not as an accidental overflow result.

## Accessibility requirements

All implementations must:

- Meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast targets.
- Preserve semantic HTML for buttons, links, headings, lists, and form fields.
- Expose labels for icon-only controls.
- Avoid color-only communication for status and progress.
- Maintain visible focus indicators across all dark surfaces.
- Support keyboard dismissal for overlays, menus, and modals.

## Implementation guidance for this repo

### What to keep

- Tailwind v4 utility approach
- `globals.css` token definitions
- Existing shell structure in `main-layout.tsx`
- Reusable UI components in `src/components/ui`

### What to improve

- Replace page-specific raw colors with token-backed utilities where feasible.
- Normalize card radii and border treatments across shared primitives.
- Bring `CustomButton`, `Dropdown`, `FormInput`, and `CardView` closer to one coherent system.
- Introduce reusable dashboard primitives instead of hand-building every panel.
- Support role-specific navigation/page composition through configuration, not duplicated layouts.

### Recommended primitive set

The app should converge on reusable primitives for:

- app shell/sidebar/header
- page title block
- stat card
- glass panel
- nested row card
- status chip
- progress bar
- button
- text link / inline action
- input
- select/dropdown
- avatar/account badge

## Anti-patterns

Do not:

- Introduce new hex values when an existing token communicates the same intent.
- Mix Chakra Petch and IBM Plex Mono arbitrarily within the same UI role.
- Create role-specific pages by copying entire layouts when composition can be data-driven.
- Use inconsistent border radii for visually related components.
- Remove focus indicators to achieve a cleaner visual style.
- Treat generated Figma code as production-ready without adapting it to existing repo patterns.

## QA checklist

Before merging any UI work, verify:

- Tokens were reused instead of hardcoded one-off values.
- Typography choices match the intended role.
- Cards use the correct family and radius.
- Selected, hover, focus, disabled, and active states exist.
- Keyboard navigation works for menus, buttons, and dropdowns.
- Status colors are semantically correct and not the only cue.
- Layout remains aligned with the authenticated app shell.
- New components are reusable and not overly page-specific.

## Figma reference

Contractor dashboard source: [InfraFund-local contractor dashboard](https://www.figma.com/design/Zq04RInLJpyFTA83nEdO4y/InfraFund-local?node-id=25140-14114&m=dev)

# InfraFund design skill

## Mission

Create implementation-ready design guidance for InfraFund UI work so engineers can build new pages and components that stay aligned with the local Figma system and this repository's established front-end patterns.

## Sources of truth

Always reconcile guidance against all of the following:

- `DESIGN.md`
- `src/app/globals.css`
- shared UI in `src/components/ui/*`
- shell components such as `src/components/header.tsx`, `src/components/sidebar.tsx`, and `src/components/main-layout.tsx`
- the active Figma file and requested node

Primary Figma reference for current dashboard system:
- contractor dashboard node `25140:14114`
- file: `InfraFund-local`

## Product style summary

InfraFund is a dark, glassy, dashboard-oriented web application with:

- neon-green primary accents
- Chakra Petch for interface hierarchy
- IBM Plex Mono for data, metadata, and wallet/system text
- rounded panels and layered dark surfaces
- restrained semantic color usage for warning, info, success, and error states

## Non-negotiable implementation rules

- Must reuse repo tokens before introducing new raw values.
- Must adapt Figma output to the existing Next.js + React + Tailwind v4 stack.
- Must prefer reusable primitives over page-specific duplicated markup.
- Must preserve keyboard accessibility and visible focus states.
- Must keep role-specific variations configuration-driven when possible.
- Must treat generated Figma code as reference, not final production code.

## Token rules

### Colors

Prefer the tokens already declared in `src/app/globals.css`, especially:

- `--color-primary`
- `--color-primary-hover`
- `--color-primary-pressed`
- `--color-primary-disabled`
- `--color-gray-50` through `--color-gray-900`
- `--color-success`
- `--color-warning`
- `--color-error`
- `--color-info`
- `--color-card-bg`
- `--color-card-bg-border`
- `--color-card-border`
- `--color-card-selected-bg`

Do not invent nearby greens, blues, or grays when these already cover the requirement.

### Typography

Use typography by role:

- Chakra Petch for page titles, section titles, nav labels, buttons, and high-emphasis interface text
- IBM Plex Mono for form data, metadata, wallet addresses, timestamps, labels, and system/supporting copy

Default expected styles:

- page title: Chakra Petch bold, around 40px when matching dashboard headers
- section/stat label: Chakra Petch medium 18px
- nav label: Chakra Petch 16px
- button label: Chakra Petch semibold 14px with tracked lettering
- supporting body/meta: IBM Plex Mono 12px to 14px

### Spacing and radius

Prefer the spacing scale 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48.

Prefer these radius tiers:

- 8px for nested items
- 12px for selected nav or compact highlighted surfaces
- 20px for major cards
- 40px for large shell containers like the sidebar

## Core component families

When writing guidance, organize components into these families:

1. App shell
2. Sidebar navigation
3. Header / account area
4. Stat cards
5. Glass panels
6. Nested item cards
7. Status chips
8. Progress indicators
9. Buttons and text actions
10. Inputs and selects
11. Avatars / wallet identity

For each family, define:

- anatomy
- typography
- spacing
- color usage
- interactive states
- accessibility expectations
- responsive behavior

## Interaction and accessibility rules

Every interactive component must define:

- default
- hover
- focus-visible
- active
- disabled
- loading when relevant

Every design rule set must include testable accessibility requirements:

- WCAG 2.2 AA contrast expectations
- keyboard reachability
- visible focus treatment
- icon-only labeling requirements
- non-color cues for status and progress
- Escape dismissal for overlays or menus where relevant

## Repo-specific guidance expectations

When giving implementation advice, explicitly align with the current repo by checking:

- whether a shared primitive already exists
- whether a token already exists in `globals.css`
- whether the shell layout already solves part of the page
- whether a component is currently inconsistent and should be normalized instead of copied

Favor convergence of existing components such as:

- `CustomButton`
- `Dropdown`
- `FormInput`
- `CardView`

## Output structure

When asked to generate guidance, use this structure:

1. Context and goal
2. Relevant existing repo patterns
3. Relevant Figma observations
4. Design tokens to use
5. Component-level rules
6. Interaction and accessibility requirements
7. Responsive behavior
8. Anti-patterns to avoid
9. Implementation notes for this repo
10. QA checklist

## Writing style

Write in a concise, confident, implementation-focused tone.

Use:

- "must" for non-negotiable rules
- "should" for recommendations
- direct references to file paths or component names when relevant

Avoid vague advice like "make it look modern" or "keep it clean" unless followed by a concrete, testable rule.

## Anti-patterns

Do not:

- output only token dumps without component guidance
- recommend raw Tailwind classes without tying them back to tokens/system intent
- ignore existing repo patterns and shared components
- propose inaccessible icon-only controls
- duplicate full page layouts when variation can be driven by data/configuration

## Success criteria

A good result:

- is reusable across multiple pages, not only one screen
- helps engineers decide what to build and how to structure it
- reflects both Figma and the real codebase
- gives explicit component/state/accessibility rules
- reduces ad hoc styling decisions in future work

# InfraFund design skill

## Mission

Create implementation-ready design guidance for InfraFund UI work so engineers can build new pages and components that stay aligned with the local Figma system and this repository's established front-end patterns.

## Sources of truth

Always reconcile guidance against all of the following:

- `DESIGN.md`
- `src/app/globals.css`
- shared UI in `src/components/ui/*`
- shell components such as `src/components/header.tsx`, `src/components/sidebar.tsx`, and `src/components/main-layout.tsx`
- the active Figma file and requested node

Primary Figma reference for current dashboard system:
- contractor dashboard node `25140:14114`
- file: `InfraFund-local`

## Product style summary

InfraFund is a dark, glassy, dashboard-oriented web application with:

- neon-green primary accents
- Chakra Petch for interface hierarchy
- IBM Plex Mono for data, metadata, and wallet/system text
- rounded panels and layered dark surfaces
- restrained semantic color usage for warning, info, success, and error states

## Non-negotiable implementation rules

- Must reuse repo tokens before introducing new raw values.
- Must adapt Figma output to the existing Next.js + React + Tailwind v4 stack.
- Must prefer reusable primitives over page-specific duplicated markup.
- Must preserve keyboard accessibility and visible focus states.
- Must keep role-specific variations configuration-driven when possible.
- Must treat generated Figma code as reference, not final production code.

## Token rules

### Colors

Prefer the tokens already declared in `src/app/globals.css`, especially:

- `--color-primary`
- `--color-primary-hover`
- `--color-primary-pressed`
- `--color-primary-disabled`
- `--color-gray-50` through `--color-gray-900`
- `--color-success`
- `--color-warning`
- `--color-error`
- `--color-info`
- `--color-card-bg`
- `--color-card-bg-border`
- `--color-card-border`
- `--color-card-selected-bg`

Do not invent nearby greens, blues, or grays when these already cover the requirement.

### Typography

Use typography by role:

- Chakra Petch for page titles, section titles, nav labels, buttons, and high-emphasis interface text
- IBM Plex Mono for form data, metadata, wallet addresses, timestamps, labels, and system/supporting copy

Default expected styles:

- page title: Chakra Petch bold, around 40px when matching dashboard headers
- section/stat label: Chakra Petch medium 18px
- nav label: Chakra Petch 16px
